claim.quote: The results indicate non-zero, Q^2 dependent, strange quark contributions and provide new information beyond that obtained in previous experiments.

key_value_text.quote: We have measured parity-violating asymmetries in elastic electron-proton scattering over the range of momentum transfers 0.12 < Q^2 < 1.0 GeV^2.

name: G0 forward angle: parity-violating asymmetries over 0.12 < Q^2 < 1.0 GeV^2
notes: Later results (HAPPEX-III, result:happex-iii-strange-vector-form-factors-2011) found the world data consistent with zero; the HAPPEX-III introduction notes that G0, A4 and others had presented evidence for non-zero strange form factors of limited significance.

summary.plain: G0 measured the electron-proton parity-violating asymmetry across a wide range of momentum transfers at once, detecting the recoiling protons. Its results indicated a non-zero, momentum-dependent strange-quark contribution, which later, more precise measurements did not confirm.
summary.technical: Parity-violating asymmetries in elastic e-p scattering over 0.12 < Q^2 < 1.0 GeV^2 using a toroidal spectrometer to detect the recoiling protons from a liquid-hydrogen target; the forward-angle data indicate non-zero, Q^2 dependent strange-quark contributions.

title: Strange Quark Contributions to Parity-Violating Asymmetries in the Forward G0 Electron-Proton Scattering Experiment
why_it_matters: Covered the whole momentum-transfer range from 0.1 to 1 GeV^2 in one experiment and motivated higher-precision follow-up measurements (HAPPEX-III, A4).
